answer.value:
Contributions of Chalukyas to Literature:
The Chalukyas encouraged literature, fostering the growth of Kannada and Sanskrit.
Kannada was their native language.
The Tripadi style of poetry developed during this period.
Many inscriptions were written in Kannada.
The inscription of Kappe Arabhatta includes Tripadi-style poetry.
Notable Sanskrit scholars includes Kavishale, Vijjika, and Akalanka, with works like Kaumudimahotsava and Hara Parvatiya composed.

questions.text: Pulakeshi II was a great king of Chalukya, Justify the statement
questions.text_as_printed: Pulakeshi II was a great king of Chalukya, Justify the statement (D)

answer.value:
Achievements of Pulakeshi II
Pulakeshi II was the most powerful emperor of the Badami Chalukyas, expanding his empire significantly.
He defeated the Pallava king Mahendravarma.
He also defeated Harshavardhana of Vardhana dynasty, earning titles like Dakshinapatheshwara and Lord of the Region Surrounded by Three Seas.
He divided his kingdom into provinces, appointing his brothers as governors.
Chinese traveler Hiuen Tsang visited the Chalukya capital.
Pulakeshi II was known as a just and compassionate ruler, beloved by his people.

questions.text: Explain the contributions of the Pallavas of Kanchi in the field of architecture.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the contributions of the Pallavas of Kanchi in the field of architecture. (A)

answer.value:
Architecture of Pallava
Pallava kings promoted the architecture along with efficient administration.
They built numerous palaces and stone temples.
Exquisite sculptures were carved from single rocks.
Stories from the Mahabharata and Bhagavata were depicted in carvings.
The sculpture called Arjuna's Penance is a masterpiece.
The Vaikuntha Perumal temple and the sea shore temple at Mahabalipuram are exemplary models of ancient Indian architecture.

questions.text: Explain the administrative system of the Badami Chalukyas.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the administrative system of the Badami Chalukyas. (A)

answer.value:
The Badami Chalukyas ruled for about 200 years.
The king actively participated in administration.
The kingdom was divided into units called Vishaya (districts).
The Vishayadhipati was in charge of these divisions.
The village was the smallest administrative unit.
The village head looked after accounts and records.

questions.text: How did the Pallavas encourage Sanskrit and Tamil languages?
questions.text_as_printed: How did the Pallavas encourage Sanskrit and Tamil languages? (D)

answer.value:
The Pallavas encouraged both Sanskrit and Tamil languages.
Kanchi was a centre of Sanskrit literature. Poets in the Pallava court included Bharavi, the author of Kiratarjuniya, and Dandi, the author of Dashakumaracharita.
King Mahendravarman himself wrote the social drama Mattavilasa Prahasana and the work Bhagavadajjukam.
During their period, verses were composed in Tamil, which became a treasure of Tamil literature. The Pallavas promoted all religions.
